title: Literature Review and Evidence Synthesis
answer: Evidence extraction, weighing the consensus, questions over your own sources, broad scans and translating between fields.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Evidence Extraction Tables
children.blurb: Evidence extraction tables are structured summaries that pull key claims, study designs, populations, interventions, outcomes, and effect sizes from primary research into a comparable grid.

children.name: Weighing the Scientific Consensus
children.blurb: Weighing the scientific consensus means assessing how much agreement exists across published AI research on a given question, and how strong that agreement is.

children.name: Questioning Your Own Sources
children.blurb: Questioning your own sources is the practice of checking the origin, methods, funding, and current status of every work you cite before treating it as evidence.

children.name: Deep Research Agents and Landscape Scans
children.blurb: Deep research agents are software systems that carry out multi-step literature search, reading, and synthesis tasks, producing landscape scans that map a field's key papers, claims, models, tools, and open questions.

children.name: Translating Between Disciplines
children.blurb: Translating between disciplines in literature review and evidence synthesis means identifying equivalent concepts, methods, and findings across fields that use different vocabularies, and mapping them so evidence can be combined.

sections.body: Artificial intelligence is being used here to extract claims from research papers into structured tables, compare findings across studies, and flag where a source may be weak or self-interested. The site's library holds 135 research papers and 10,767 extracted claims, which gives a sense of the scale involved. This is not a theoretical exercise; the tools read actual PDFs, pull out sentences that state a finding, and record the method and sample size where possible. The work also includes broad scans that search across many papers at once and attempts to translate findings between fields that use different vocabulary.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is uneven. Extraction from clean, born-digital PDFs is fairly reliable, but tables, equations, and scanned older papers still cause errors. Weighing the scientific consensus is not solved; models can count how many papers agree or disagree, but they cannot yet judge the quality of evidence or detect subtle conflicts of interest. Questioning sources is also limited because a model can check citations and funding statements but cannot know what a researcher left out. Translating between disciplines remains hard because the same word can mean different things in different fields, and no current system handles that reliably.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader would start with Evidence Extraction Tables to see how claims are pulled from papers and what gets lost in that process. Weighing the Scientific Consensus then explains how those extracted claims are compared and where the numbers can mislead. Questioning Your Own Sources is the page for checking whether a paper you rely on is trustworthy, including its funding and citation patterns. Deep Research Agents and Landscape Scans covers broader automated searches across many papers, and Translating Between Disciplines addresses the problem of moving findings between fields without losing meaning.
